newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian police fear 250 killed in train blast.
newsitem.headline: Indian police fear 250 killed in train blast.

text.p: At least 250 people were feared killed in a bomb explosion on a packed train in India's northeastern state of Assam on Monday, police said.
"The engine and four bogeys (carriages) were blown up in the explosion," an Assam police spokesman told Reuters in Calcutta by telephone. "A minimum of 250 people are feared to be killed."
Police said it was not immediately clear who may have planted the bomb in the Delhi-bound Brahmaputra Mail which had left Assam's Kokrajhar station when the explosion occurred.
The blast came a day after tribal Bodo guerrillas blew up a road bridge that formed the main link between India's northeast regions and the rest of the country, injuring seven people.

A police officer told Reuters on Monday that ethnic Bodo rebels blasted the bridge over a small river at Rakhaldubi, between the towns of Bijni and Bongaigaon on National Highway 31 in the tea and oil-rich state of Assam.

Activists representing Bodo tribesmen living north of the Brahmaputra river want a homeland within India in the state of Assam, but an extremist fringe, the Bodoland Army, has been fighting for a separate nation since 1989.
